correctness.rationale: The complete proof establishes that a selected rook-graph vertex set is bipartite iff its K_m,n incidence graph has row/column degrees <=2; the extension criterion shows maximality iff no missing edge joins two unsaturated vertices. Simultaneous unsaturated vertices force exactly one edge between them and a two-regular residual with m=n. Otherwise the shorter side must saturate. A labeled path/cycle decomposition gives exp(y + sum x^k y^{k+1}/2 + sum (xy)^k/(2k)), hence the exact coefficient formula; boundary n=2 is included. The extracted Python verifier independently constructs rook graph two-coloring for small boards and compares maximal families and rational EGF coefficients over eleven parameter instances.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches and full available primary-text inspections distinguish the new all-parameter labeled facet enumerator and sharp pure/nonpure square transition from pre-existing general maximal-subgraph listing algorithms and finite homotopy/face counts. The exact K3,4, K3,5 and K4,4 numerical results are already known and expressly excluded as novelty claims. Search absence is not a universal priority proof; possible unindexed general facet enumeration remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named exact facet formula may predate this account.
Reiner–Roberts (2000) was examined in selected PDF passages/page images rather than in its entirety; its rational-homology results do not directly imply an all-facet count.
A computer enumeration of finitely many boards is only corroboration; the argument for all sizes is in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The parameter-general facet enumerator and sharp pure/nonpure boundary describe natural combinatorial-topological complexes, not just a small-n census or a known extremum. They also enumerate every maximal induced bipartite vertex set in Cartesian products of complete graphs and specify exact size distributions for arbitrary rectangular and square boards. These quantities are meaningful in simplicial purity and maximal-solution enumeration and are not implied by the cited finite homotopy descriptions.
